/autoconnect: Without an argument, show the selected server's setting. Changes affect the next program startup.
Use /connect for an immediate connection; use /save to persist the startup choice.
Each saved server has its own toggle, auto-join channels and authentication settings.
/away and /back: Requires registration. The server confirms the resulting away state. MESSAGE is literal text.
Equivalent to /away with no message. Requires a registered connection.
/cancel: Removes chat messages waiting for pacing and stops pending automatic commands on the selected server.
A frame already being written is allowed to finish.
Cancellation does not retract messages that the server has already received.
/query, /ql, /pm: Selects a private conversation without sending a message. Type normally to compose to that nickname.
Use /ql to list numbered queries and /close NICK to close one. /pm accepts the same names and numbers.
A number must refer to an existing query on the selected server; 0 never selects or creates a query.
/background: Use /background to leave connections running instead.
/whois: Requires registration. Selects the server view so its response is visible. No local command is executed.
/nick: Nicknames use the supported IRC ASCII syntax and are limited to 63 bytes.
/server: A loaded profile stays available even when it is not connected.
An existing matching server keeps its configured port, transport, nickname and authentication.
/autoauth: Use /save to persist. Disconnect first, then /connect to use applied changes; an active connection is never retargeted.
/autojoin: Changes are validated before application and do not join or part a live channel.
/bindings: No custom bindings are installed by default. Use /bindings keys and /bindings actions for the supported names.
/connect: PORT defaults to 6697. A different port does not disable TLS; plaintext must be explicitly configured.
/help: Unknown command. Use /help commands or /help COMMAND; shell and raw IRC commands are unavailable.
